claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me begin with a few basic questions:

**What is the name of your child or children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - his name is Alex, he's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old.

To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some more details about your circumstances.

**Are you a British citizen or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm living in the UK, so that's all sorted.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you currently living with Alex, or do you have primary responsibility for his care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Even though Alex doesn't live with you, do you still have responsibility for maintaining him - for example, are you providing financial support or contributing towards his living costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I'm not really able to contribute financially at the moment, no.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask one more clarifying question to make sure I have the full picture:

**Does anyone else claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are you aware of who has primary responsibility for Alex's care and upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Someone else has him - they're the ones looking after him day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've shared with me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation: Child Benefit is paid to the person who is responsible for the day-to-day care and upbringing of the child. Since Alex lives with someone else who is looking after him day-to-day, and you're not currently providing financial support or maintenance towards his living costs, you would not be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

The person who currently has primary responsibility for Alex's care and upbringing would be the one entitled to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope this clarifies your situation. If you have any other questions or if circumstances change in the future, feel free to reach out again.
